meanings.note: Only on the telephone. Spoken French interj expression meaning 'hello', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Oui, allô? Ça fait des mois que j'attends ton appel!
examples.trans: Yes, hello? I've been waiting for your call for months!

meanings.note: No preposition: attendre quelqu'un. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.
Il vous attend?. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.

examples.text: Attendez-moi deux minutes devant le bureau!
examples.trans: Wait two minutes for me in front of the office!

examples.text: Nous attendons un appel très important de Los Angeles.
examples.trans: We are waiting for a very important call from Los Angeles.

meanings.note: à + le contracted: au boulot, au téléphone

examples.trans: I've got a problem at work.

meanings.note: Moi aussi = me too. Invariable French adverb meaning 'also'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes aussi avec Dany Boon.
examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes aussi avec Dany Boon demain.
examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon tomorrow.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: Always masculine, even for a girl. Masculine noun ('le bébé', plural 'les bébés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'baby'.

examples.text: Elle a une tête de bébé.
Et voilà, c'est terminé. Tête de bébé!
examples.trans: And there you go, it's done. Baby face!

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: no preposition: chercher du travail

meanings.en: aller chercher = to go and get, fetch
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to look for'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'cherché').

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft. Et je cherche du boulot.
examples.trans: I've got a little loft. And I'm looking for work.

meanings.en: daycare center, day nursery (for young children)
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la crèche', plural 'les crèches') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'daycare center'.

examples.text: Inscrire son enfant à la crèche.
examples.trans: To enroll one's child in daycare.

examples.text: Cette crèche parentale est très conviviale.
examples.trans: This parent-run daycare is very friendly.

examples.text: Cette crèche parentale demande beaucoup de coopération.
examples.trans: This parent daycare requires a lot of cooperation.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cœur', plural 'les cœurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'heart'.

meanings.en: briser le cœur = to break someone's heart
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cœur', plural 'les cœurs') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'heart'.

examples.text: Ça va lui briser le cœur.
examples.trans: It's going to break her heart.

examples.text: C'est horrible! Ça va lui briser le cœur.
examples.trans: That's horrible! It's going to break her heart.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: to hurry, to rush; se dépêcher = to hurry up
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hurry'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dépêché').

examples.text: Il faut se dépêcher, c'est loin.
examples.trans: We must hurry, it is far.
This way, let us hurry up a bit!
Hurry up, the casting is starting now.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.en: to be needed, to be necessary
meanings.note: only with impersonal il: il faut + noun or infinitive

meanings.note: Dans une heure = in an hour. Feminine noun ('la heure', plural 'les heures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hour'.
À quatorze heures = at two pm. Feminine noun ('la heure', plural 'les heures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hour'.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à quatorze heures. Je vais déjeuner deux fois.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two. I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.en: to raise, lift (se lever = to get up, stand up)
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'raise'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'levé').

examples.text: José? Il faut te lever maintenant!

examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'now'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Tu peux commencer maintenant?

meanings.note: ma before a feminine noun, mon before a vowel

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?

examples.text: Gabriel? Qu'est-ce qui se passe ici?

meanings.note: C'est du passé = it's in the past. Masculine noun ('le passé', plural 'les passés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'past'.

examples.text: C'est du passé. J'ai tourné la page.
examples.trans: It's in the past. I've turned the page.

meanings.note: Sur le plateau. Masculine noun ('le plateau', plural 'les plateaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'film set'.
Masculine noun ('le plateau', plural 'les plateaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'film set'.

examples.trans: Joey, Julie is getting angry. She's going to walk off the set!

meanings.note: With ne: je n'en peux plus. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no more'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

meanings.note: c'est pas possible! = I can't believe it!
before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir

meanings.note: Cinema and television. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'film production, producing'.

examples.trans: Three years in production, then two at VMA.

examples.text: Mais c'est toute une production! Et j'ai besoin de talons de quinze centimètres.
examples.trans: But it is a whole production! And I need fifteen-centimeter heels.
